worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in the known information gives

$$
2+(-5)={\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,⇒\,{\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-3.
$$

Finally, compute the desired integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{6}(2f(x)+4)\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{1}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x+4{\int }_{1}^{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2(-3)+4\cdot x\,{|}_{1}^{6} \\  & =-6+4(6-1) \\  & =-6+20 \\  & =14\end{aligned}
$$
